record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Finite invariant sets and separability via polynomial invariants
record.original_question: For local-unitary entanglement invariants, determine finite complete sets of polynomial invariants for specified Alice and Bob Hilbert-space dimensions, extend the problem to multipartite states including pure multipartite states, and decide whether separability can be characterized, or at least usefully approximated by necessary or sufficient criteria, using a polynomial invariant f with f(rho) >= 0 corresponding to separability, possibly with f depending on the dimensions.

evidence.quote:
But we may add some further, closely related problems:
• Given the dimensions of Alices’s and Bob’s Hilbert spaces, name a finite set of invariants which is already complete.
• Do all this for multi-partite states. In this case even the case of pure states is not obvious.
• Decide whether the set of separable states can be described in terms of a polynomial invariant f, such that f(ρ) ≥ 0 is equivalent to separability.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider finite-dimensional quantum systems. For a bipartite system with Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ of dimensions $d_A = \dim\mathcal{H}_A$ and $d_B = \dim\mathcal{H}_B$, the local unitary group $U(d_A)\times U(d_B)$ acts on density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$ by $\rho \mapsto (U_A\otimes U_B)\rho(U_A\otimes U_B)^\dagger$. A polynomial local-unitary (LU) invariant is a polynomial function in the matrix entries of $\rho$ that is constant on each orbit of this action. A set $\{f_1,\dots,f_N\}$ of LU-invariants is called complete if it separates the orbits, i.e., $f_i(\rho)=f_i(\sigma)$ for all $i$ implies that $\rho$ and $\sigma$ lie in the same LU-orbit. A density operator $\rho$ is called separable if it can be written as a convex combination $\rho=\sum_k p_k\,\rho_k^A\otimes\rho_k^B$ with $p_k\geq 0$, $\sum_k p_k=1$, and $\rho_k^A,\rho_k^B$ density operators on $\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B$ respectively. The analogous notions extend to multipartite systems $\mathcal{H}_{A_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{H}_{A_n}$ with local unitary group $U(d_{A_1})\times\cdots\times U(d_{A_n})$, in particular to the case of pure multipartite states.

Address the following problems:

(a) For specified dimensions $d_A,d_B$, exhibit an explicit finite complete set of polynomial LU-invariants for mixed states on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$.

(b) Carry out the analogous program in the multipartite setting, including the case of pure multipartite states.

(c) Decide whether the set of separable states can be characterized by a polynomial LU-invariant $f$ (possibly depending on the dimensions) such that $f(\rho)\geq 0$ is equivalent to $\rho$ being separable. If no such exact characterization exists, determine whether useful necessary or sufficient separability criteria can be obtained from polynomial LU-invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: Finite complete sets of polynomial LU-invariants are known in several cases: 18 generators for two qubits (Makhlin), and complete sets for various classes including non-degenerate bipartite mixed states in arbitrary dimensions. Coefficient-matrix-based invariants have been developed for general bipartite and multipartite systems, but a unified explicit complete set for arbitrary dimensions and arbitrary multipartite states is not fully settled. The separability characterization question — whether there exists a polynomial LU-invariant $f$ with $f(\rho)\ge 0$ iff $\rho$ is separable — is listed as still open on the Open Quantum Problems project page.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial entanglement invariants – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Decide whether the set of separable states can be described in terms of a polynomial invariant f, such that f(ρ)≥0 is equivalent to separability. There are many weaker versions of this problem.
status_evidence.claim: Separability via a polynomial LU-invariant remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Local unitary equivalence of arbitrary-dimensional multipartite quantum states
status_evidence.snippet: Local unitary invariants found for arbitrary-dimensional bipartite quantum states, used as necessary conditions for LU equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made on finite invariants in bipartite and multipartite settings.

status_evidence.title: On the Ring of Local Unitary Invariants for Mixed X-States of Two Qubits
status_evidence.snippet: Makhlin: the ring of polynomial LU-invariants for two-qubit mixed states has 18 generators.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit complete sets are known in low dimensions.
